c.tagline: New Zealand's Great Lake – geothermal steam, Huka Falls, and volcano trails.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis and a limited number of Uber drivers operate; book by phone or app, especially late at night when supply is thin.

emergency.note: 111 is New Zealand's single emergency number for police, fire and ambulance.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Lock vehicles and hide valuables at trailhead and lakeside car parks, where opportunistic break-ins occur.

hood_desc: The compact, walkable heart on the lake's northern edge, packed with cafes, bars, the i-SITE and the marina where boat cruises and the Huka jet depart; best for first-timers who want everything on foot.
A relaxed lakeside strip a few minutes south of town with a swimming beach, the DeBretts hot pools nearby and easy reach of Huka Falls; suits couples and families wanting the lake without the bustle.
A quiet, upscale residential bay across the water with the area's best sunset lake-and-mountain views and sandy swimming beaches; a peaceful base with a car.
A leafy suburb just across the Control Gates Bridge and the Waikato River trails, walkable to town yet calmer; handy for cyclists and longer self-catered stays.
A resort-style village 20 minutes northwest with a sheltered marina and the Jack Nicklaus golf course, backed by the Great Lake Trail; suits golfers, boaties and hikers wanting seclusion.
lodging: Millennium Hotel and Resort Manuels Taupo

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink.

transit.hours: Local bus and shuttle services run mainly in daytime; there is no night network, so most visitors drive or use taxis after hours.
transit.note: Taupō is a small lakeside town with no rail or tram; a compact local bus service plus taxis cover the town, but a car is by far the easiest way to reach Huka Falls, the Tongariro trailheads and the wider lake.
transit.pay: Local bus fares are paid in cash to the driver (a few dollars); there is no smartcard system.

bus: InterCity coaches to Auckland, Rotorua, Wellington and Napier

transit.m: Taxi or shuttle to the town centre (10-12 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not expected in New Zealand; staff are paid a full wage, though rounding up for exceptional service is welcome.

food.name: Lake Taupo trout, cooked by a chef
food.desc: Trout cannot legally be bought or sold in New Zealand, so you catch your own on the lake and a restaurant cooks it for you, whole-baked, pan-fried or smoked.

places.name: Vine Eatery and Bar
places.note: Well known for cooking guests' catch, including whole-baked trout with olives and herbs.

places.name: Plateau Bar and Eatery
places.note: Central bar-restaurant that will prepare your fishing charter's catch on request.

places.name: Taupo Boat Harbour charters
places.note: Where the trout charters leave from; skippers arrange a restaurant to cook what you land.

food.name: New Zealand lamb
food.desc: Grass-fed lamb rump or slow-cooked shoulder, usually served with kumara, seasonal greens and a red-wine or mint jus. A staple of every Taupo menu.

places.name: The Brantry
places.note: Set seasonal menus in a 1950s house; lamb and venison are recurring highlights.

places.name: Bistro Lago
places.note: Local-produce bistro that has become a favourite for a special-occasion dinner.

places.name: Edgewater Restaurant
places.note: Lakeside dining room doing New Zealand classics with views to the Tongariro peaks.

food.name: Hangi
food.desc: Maori earth-oven feast: meat, kumara, pumpkin and cabbage steamed for hours in a covered pit until smoky and falling apart.

places.name: Wairakei Terraces
places.note: Geothermal park north of town running an evening Maori cultural show with a hangi dinner.

places.name: Tamaki Maori Village
places.note: The best-known hangi and concert experience in the region, an hour north of Taupo.

places.name: Te Puia
places.note: Geyser park with a long-established hangi buffet and cultural performance.

food.name: Whitebait fritters
food.desc: Tiny translucent inanga bound in egg and fried into a thin omelette, eaten with lemon and white bread. Strictly seasonal from spring.

places.name: Vine Eatery and Bar
places.note: Sharing-plate menu that picks up seasonal New Zealand specialities when they appear.

places.name: Plateau Bar and Eatery
places.note: Kiwi pub-bistro cooking; a likely place to find fritters in whitebait season.

places.name: Edgewater Restaurant
places.note: New Zealand classics by the lake, including seasonal seafood plates.

food.name: Venison
food.desc: Farmed Cervena venison from the central North Island, served pink with beetroot, juniper or berry sauces. Leaner and sweeter than European game.

places.name: The Brantry
places.note: Three-course seasonal menus that regularly feature venison plated with modern flair.

places.name: Bistro Lago
places.note: Curated local-produce menu with New Zealand game and beef alongside the fish.

places.name: Plateau Bar and Eatery
places.note: Relaxed spot for venison and craft beer after a day on the mountains.

food.name: Hokey pokey ice cream
food.desc: New Zealand's own flavour: vanilla ice cream studded with shards of golden honeycomb toffee, best eaten in a cone by the lakefront.

places.name: Taupo lakefront ice cream shops
places.note: Cluster of parlours facing the lake; hokey pokey is on every board.

places.name: Storehouse
places.note: Popular central cafe in a converted warehouse, good for sweets and coffee.

places.name: L'Arte Cafe
places.note: Mosaic garden cafe just out of town, a local favourite for cake and ice cream.

food.name: Taupo craft beer
food.desc: The central plateau has its own small breweries pouring pale ales, pilsners and stouts, often named for the region's fishing and mountains.

places.name: Lakeman Brewing Co
places.note: Taupo's own brewery and taproom; fishing-themed beers poured at source.

places.name: Crafty Trout Brewing
places.note: Bavarian-style brewpub on the Tongariro River, worth the drive for the tanks and food.

places.name: Plateau Bar and Eatery
places.note: Central bar with a rotating New Zealand craft tap list.

food.name: Flat white
food.desc: The New Zealand coffee order: a double espresso under steamed milk with a thin layer of microfoam, poured in independent cafes across town.

places.name: Storehouse
places.note: Industrial-style cafe that anchors Taupo's coffee scene; brunch queues at weekends.

places.name: Spoon and Paddle
places.note: Neighbourhood cafe well liked for its coffee and generous brunch plates.

places.name: L'Arte Cafe
places.note: Artist-run cafe and sculpture garden, a quieter place for a morning flat white.

landmarks: Huka Falls
New Zealand's most-visited natural attraction, where the Waikato River funnels into a narrow gorge and explodes over an 11-metre ledge in a torrent of turquoise.
Lake Taupō
A vast caldera lake the size of Singapore, born of a super-volcanic eruption, offering sailing, trout fishing and snow-capped volcano views across its glittering expanse.
Mine Bay Māori Rock Carvings
A 14-metre likeness of navigator Ngātoroirangi gazes from lakeside cliffs, carved in the 1970s and reachable only by boat, kayak or sailing tour.
Craters of the Moon (Karapiti)
Boardwalks wind through a hissing lunar landscape of steaming craters, bubbling mud and sulphur-stained earth in one of Taupō's most otherworldly geothermal fields.
Aratiatia Rapids
Watch dam gates unleash a scheduled flood that transforms a dry rocky gorge into churning white water within minutes, a spectacle featured in The Hobbit.
Spa Thermal Park and Otumuheke Stream
Locals' favourite free soak, where naturally hot water tumbles into the cool Waikato River, creating blissful bathing pools beside a scenic riverside park.
Wairakei Terraces
Man-made silica terraces recreate the lost Pink and White Terraces, cascading steaming water into milky-blue pools where adults can bathe in mineral-rich geothermal springs.
Taupō Museum
This lakeside museum tells the region's volcanic and Māori story, showcasing a carved meeting house, vintage trout-fishing memorabilia and the award-winning Ora garden.
AC Baths
A public thermal swimming and sauna complex in the town centre, tapping the same geothermal water that warms the wider Taupō basin.
Taupō Bungy
A cantilevered platform jutting from a cliff at Hell's Gate on the Waikato River, launching jumpers 47 metres above the rapids.

train.note: No passenger rail serves Taupō; the nearest railheads are in Hamilton and Palmerston North.

bus.note: InterCity and Skip coaches connect Taupō with Auckland (~4.5 hrs), Rotorua (~1 hr), Napier (~2 hrs) and Wellington (~5.5 hrs).

ferry.note: No ferry service; boats on Lake Taupō are sightseeing cruises only.

full.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing
full.blurb: One of the world's great day hikes, crossing volcanic craters and emerald lakes in Tongariro National Park.

full.name: Orakei Korako
full.blurb: A hidden geothermal valley of silica terraces reached by boat, about 30 minutes north.

full.name: Rotorua
full.blurb: Geothermal and Māori-culture hub an hour north, with geysers, spa pools and bubbling mud.
